Title: Why Ian Forrestal is so good

Messages.Author: XZealot
Messages.Body:
Ian Forrestal's special text.

Ian can play cards of any Discipline as though he has the basic level
of that Discipline. Master Discipline cards played on him grant the
superior level of that Discipline.

This is actually two DISTINCT abilities.

1) The first sentance is the ability to "emulate" any one discipline
that he doesn't possess at inferior.

2) The second sentance is the "Instant Superiors just add water".

So Ian Forrestal could play a Superior Elemental Stocism (which
requires inferior obfuscate and Supeior Fortitude) with only a single
Fortitude skill card.

Did everyone else already know that?

Another example of Ian's 2 separate abilities:

If Ian Forestal is acting, he can play basic Alacrity for stealth, because he
can "emulate" celerity. But a blocking minion can play Rooftop Shadow,
because he doesn't actually *have* celerity.
But if Ian Forestal gets just one Celerity skillcard, then he can not only
play superior Alacrity, but is immune to Rooftop Shadow because he now
*actually has* superior Celerity.

Additionally, Ian can only "fake out" one discipline at a time (so he can
play basic Read the Winds because he already actually has auspex).

But he can even fake a discipline if he is Clan Impersonated to Kiasyd and
uses the Grandest Trick, because he's now an ally with the special ability
"can play cards requiring any basic discipline [as a vampire of capacity 1]."

This is not meant as an example of "hot tech", but merely as an explanation
of how the ability works :)
